title: Stable primary navigation
summary: Keep the product's highest-frequency destinations in a predictable primary navigation structure instead of reshuffling them between screens.
problem: Users lose orientation when core destinations move, disappear behind context-specific controls, or compete with secondary links.
use_when: A product has several recurring top-level destinations
Users revisit the same major areas across sessions
avoid_when: The experience is a short linear transaction with no need to switch sections
There is only one meaningful destination
rationale: Primary navigation should describe information architecture, not every available action.

prefer_alternatives_if: The flow is intentionally linear and leaving the step would create data loss or confusion
use_if: A product has several recurring top-level destinations
Users revisit the same major areas across sessions

requirements: Expose navigation landmarks and meaningful link names.
Make current location perceivable without relying on color alone.
keyboard: Navigation items follow normal tab order unless a documented composite-widget pattern is used.

responsive: Transform presentation at smaller widths without hiding access to core destinations.
